transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just keep going back over my jobs again and again. 

I'm an electrician, and lately... I'll finish up, but then I have to check the breakers, make sure the labels are exactly right, check the torque marks, even take photos of the panel just to prove to myself it's done right. Sometimes I'll actually drive all the way back to a site after I've left just to check it one more time. It's getting to the point where a really simple install is taking me way longer than it should, and people at work are starting to notice.
When you feel you have to go back and check, is it because an unwanted thought keeps popping up that something could be wrong or unsafe?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Even after I know I've checked a panel or a disconnect, this thought just keeps barging in on me. I'll start thinking that maybe I missed one loose neutral wire, or... or that I left something in a way that could start a fire. I really try to shake it off and just drive, but the thought just follows me all the way home.
Do you feel that all this checking is excessive, even though you still feel driven to do it?

Yeah, definitely. I mean... I know I'm good at my job, and I've been doing this a long time. So logically, I know going back to check the same breaker three or four times is just... it's too much. It doesn't make sense. But knowing that doesn't really help. I still just feel like I have to do it anyway, or I won't be able to let it go.
About how much time does this checking take up for you in a typical day?

I'm not exactly sure, to be honest. I haven't really timed it or anything. I mean, it kind of depends on the day and how many jobs I'm running. 

If I'm just standing at the panel checking the labels and the breakers a few extra times before I pack up my tools, maybe it's just a chunk of minutes here and there. But if it's one of those days where I actually get in the truck and drive all the way back to a site... that obviously eats up a lot more time. So yeah, I don't have an exact number for you. I just know it's enough to really throw off my schedule.
On a typical day, do these checking rituals take more than an hour in total?

I'm really not sure if it hits a full hour every single day. If I had to guess... maybe? Like I said, I don't really clock it. 

If I'm just lingering at the breaker panel before I leave, it's probably not a whole hour. But if it's one of those days where I actually turn the truck around and drive back to a job site... then yeah, that definitely pushes it way past an hour. It just really depends on how bad it gets that day.
Outside of this checking, have you generally been a perfectionistic person who likes things done in a very rigid, exact way?

Not really, no. I mean, I take pride in my work, obviously—you kind of have to as an electrician so things don't catch fire. But I wouldn't say I'm rigid about everything else in my life. 

Outside of this thing with the panels, I'm actually pretty laid back. My garage is a bit of a mess, my house isn't perfectly organized or anything like that. So, no, I don't think I'm a perfectionist overall. It's really just... just this specific issue at work.
Did this checking problem start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've tried to figure that out myself, but... nothing really comes to mind. There wasn't any big shock or major change at home, or some accident on the job or anything like that. 

It just sort of... started happening. Maybe it crept up on me over time, but I really can't point to one specific event that kicked it all off.
Outside of work, do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different everyday things?

No, not really. I mean, I have the normal stuff... bills, you know, keeping the house up, but nothing crazy. I don't sit around stressing about everyday things. Like I said, it's really just the electrical panels at work that get to me. Everything else is pretty normal.
